npcs.name: Gigia Ghisolfi
npcs.title: Hazelnut farmer

lines: The groves are back in touch with the world. Aunt Teresa, the old tree by the gate, has been telling everyone.
Shh. I'm telling the hazelnut trees about the weather. They worry.
Ah, the Geometra. The trees were asking if you're the kind who measures twice.

sleepy: Zzz… no, Aunt Teresa, you can't drop your nuts early… oh. It's you.

topics.label: Do you really talk to your trees?
lines: Of course. They never talk back. That's what makes them good company.
Every one has a name. Mostly my aunts. The trees don't mind, and my aunts never found out.

topics.label: What's across the stream?
lines: My groves. Hazelnut trees, my seed shed, and the best view of the Alps in the valley.
Since the storm took the crossing I can't get the cart over. The trees must think I've left them.

topics.label: How do the garden beds work?
lines: Plant a pumpkin seed, water it, then leave it alone. Pumpkins hate being watched.
Water again when the soil goes pale. In a while you'll have pumpkins the size of the Sindaco's opinion of himself.

gifts.line: Seeds from my best pumpkin. It won a prize in 1987 and has never let me forget it.

npcs.name: Elio Fusibile
npcs.title: Electrician

lines: I wired a lamp shaped like a cathedral today. Just to see. Don't tell anyone. Actually… tell a few people.
Oh. H-hello. Sorry, I was practising saying hello to the fuse box.
My shop is all boxes and cables. An electrician without a shop is just a man with a lot of wire in his pockets.

sleepy: *yawn* I dreamt of a chandelier made of neon spaghetti. It was beautiful.

topics.label: What would you love to build?
lines: Officially? Sensible sockets. Safe light switches.
Secretly…
A chandelier in the shape of the bell tower. A staircase that lights up as you climb it. A sign for the bakery that says CAKE in every colour there is.
Please forget I said any of that.

topics.label: What happened to your shop?
lines: The roof leaked on the fuse box, the fuse box sulked, and I closed for 'a few days'. That was three years ago.
If someone helped me set it up again… a workbench, a couple of seats, some lamps, some shelves. And copper wire. Always copper wire.

topics.label: Why does everyone smile at your name?
lines: Fusibile. It means fuse. It's a very old family name, and it was fine until 1990.
There was a football match. Every television in the village was on. I was testing a new kind of extension cord. We don't talk about it.

gifts.line: I drew you a lamp. It's shaped like a hazelnut. On purpose.

npcs.name: Sindaco Dalmasso
npcs.title: Commendator Gustavo Dalmasso, mayor of Monteforchetta

lines: The city bus is running! I have written the speech. Twice. The second one has pauses for applause.
Ah, our Geometra! Walk with me. Slowly. People should see us together.
{name}! Have you seen my campaign poster? Don't answer. Everyone has seen it. It's on the bell tower.

sleepy: I am not asleep. I am listening to the will of the people with my eyes closed.

topics.label: Why is the town hall in a castle?
lines: Because the castle was free and the old town hall had a leak. Also, a mayor should have battlements.
The counts who built it left in 1802. I like to think they left it to me.

topics.label: What's at the south end of the village?
lines: The belvedere. The finest view in the province, by my own decree. On a clear day you can see the Alps.
Aldo wants to turn his buses round there. I want a statue there. We may both be right.

topics.label: Any emergencies today?
lines: A pigeon sat on my poster this morning. Directly on my face. I have written to the prefecture.
They have not replied. I take that as support.

topics.label: When is the election?
lines: Soon enough to matter, and far enough away to fix the fountain first. Timing, {name}, is everything in politics.
Every bridge you build is a bridge I promised. I want you to know that I am very proud of us.

gifts.line: The plan for a statue, for citizens of distinction. You may model it on yourself. I modelled mine on me.

npcs.name: Fede Cauda
npcs.title: Computer whiz

lines: The fountain photo is going on the website! As soon as the modem stops screaming. It's very nearly a website.
Hi. Do you know anything about modems? No? Nobody does. That's the problem with this village.
Careful, that cable is plugged into something. I'm not sure what. Leave it.

sleepy: Zzz… page cannot be displayed… zzz… try again later…

topics.label: Do you live here?
lines: Born here, stuck here. My parents have the farm on the castle road. I have the only computer for twenty kilometres.
I'm saving up for a faster modem. At this rate I'll have one by the year 2000. Oh. That's soon.

topics.label: How do the old machines work?
lines: The fountain used to run off the mill channel. A waterwheel turns, shafts and gear boxes carry the power, and a pump pushes the water through pipes.
It's like a network, only wet. Every connector has to line up, or nothing talks to anything.

topics.label: What are you working on?
lines: A website for Monteforchetta. A home page, a picture of the castle, and a counter that says how many people have visited.
So far it says three. Two of them were me.

gifts.line: Spare parts from my old computer. Some of them were even spare before I took it apart.

npcs.name: Ornella Tealdi
npcs.title: Baker

lines: The bakery is boar-free. One bread roll has a tooth mark in it. I'm selling it as 'rustic'.
Out! Out! Not you. The boars. They come up from the woods every morning and help themselves.
Tealdi Bakery is open. The bins round the back are not. The boars have learned to read the sign.

sleepy: Mm… the dough has to rise at four… so do I… unfortunately.

topics.label: Boars?
lines: Three of them. They smell the chestnut bread and walk straight in like regular customers.
They don't pay, they don't queue, and the big one looks at me like I owe him money.

topics.label: What do you bake?
lines: Bread before dawn, breadsticks by eight, and on Sundays my hazelnut cake. People used to drive up from the valley for it.
Before the road washed out. Now they phone and ask me to describe it.

gifts.line: A slice of hazelnut cake, still warm. Don't tell the boars.

npcs.name: Aldo Barbero
npcs.title: Bus driver, known as Tornanti

lines: The turnaround is ready, and so am I. Climb aboard whenever you like. Mind the second step, it has opinions.
Did I ever tell you about the bend where I met a wolf, a priest and a cheese lorry? All at once. All going uphill.
Every bend on this road has a story, {name}. Forty-seven bends. I have forty-eight stories.

sleepy: Zzz… next stop… zzz… everybody off… zzz…

topics.label: Tell me a story from the road.
lines: One winter I drove the whole valley in fog so thick I steered by the smell of the bakeries.
I arrived at the right village. Wrong valley, but the right village.

topics.label: Where does your bus go?
lines: Down the valley, along the river and on to the city, once there's a proper turnaround up here for the new bus.
The new bus is two metres longer than the old one. The man from the region calls that progress. I call it a lot of reversing.

npcs.name: Barnaby Sprocket
npcs.title: Master Clockmaker

lines: Tick, tock! Listen to her go. Thirty years I waited for that sound, and it took a stranger with a waterwheel.
Ah! A visitor! You must be the builder my niece Tilly keeps writing about. Pages and pages. With diagrams.
Welcome, welcome. Mind the springs on the floor, they bite.

sleepy: Zzz… the escapement… needs… a nap…

topics.label: What happened here?
lines: Every machine on the cove ran on the old Great Engine. One stormy night it jammed, and everything stopped at once. The clock, the lighthouse, even the gulls looked confused.
We've been fixing things one by one ever since. Slowly. Very, very slowly.

topics.label: You know Tilly?
lines: My niece! She takes after me: brilliant, untidy, and absolutely forbidden from touching the big lever.

gifts.line: My own lever design. Do try not to pull it just to see what happens. Everyone does.

npcs.name: Juniper Flint
npcs.title: Lighthouse Keeper

lines: Did you see her last night? Sweeping the whole bay. The fishing boats came home singing.
Evening, or morning, or whatever it is. Hard to tell when your lighthouse is dark.
I'm Juniper. I keep the light. Well. I keep the lighthouse. The light is… currently resting.

sleepy: Mmh… one more lap of the lamp room…

topics.label: Why is it dark?
lines: The lamp's turned by wind, through a drive on the south side of the tower. The old windmill blew down years ago.
Build me a new one up on the cape and connect it, and she'll shine again.

gifts.line: Lighthouse keeper's luck: the best catch of the week, and a crystal I found in the lamp room.

npcs.name: Hazel Rivet
npcs.title: Smith & Trader

lines: Hear that roar? That's a happy furnace. Thanks to you, the cove's got gears again.
Welcome to Rivet's Forge! Gears, springs, plans, and a very warm floor.
If you've got metal, I'm buying. If you need parts, I'm selling. Everybody wins, especially me.

sleepy: The forge sleeps, and so do I. Come back at sunrise!

topics.label: About the forge
lines: Hottest fire on the cove. Too hot, some say. Those people have no eyebrows.

gifts.line: A pump design of my own. Pumps water uphill if you power it from the side. Physics hates it.
